name: Tonnarella
desc: The old quarter of a port on a rocky headland: tall palazzi, stair lanes, laundry lines, and a lighthouse gone dark since the February storm.

meter.name: The changeover
meter.about: Tonnarella is changing its lire for euros, one shop, one queue and one grumble at a time. Every request you finish moves the changeover on: fifteen points for the big ones, four for the others, one for each piece of washing back on its line. At 100% the last lira is spent.

milestones.title: Prices in both.
milestones.desc: Nicolò hands out euro converters. Every price, in every place, shows lire and euros, lire first.

milestones.title: Nonna buys a converter.
milestones.desc: She still checks it against her head. Davide finds you a fisherman's wool cap at the back of the chandlery.

milestones.title: Euros first.
milestones.desc: The euro becomes the main figure on every price. Your roof terrace grows onto the next roof.

milestones.title: Baciccia gives in.
milestones.desc: He frames his last 1,000-lire note over his stall. Rosetta knits you a navy fisherman's sweater, and a vine goes up on your terrace.

milestones.title: The last lira.
milestones.desc: Lire are gone, in every place. Nicolò gives you a framed 1,000-lire note for your wall.
